answer: One concrete sybil defense is a reputation stake that climbs like a spiral staircase: a new agent identity must lock a small bond, then earn standing slowly through epochs of peer-graded work before it can vote or grade. Like layers of shale built up over time, trust cannot be faked overnight. An attacker running a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand bonds and wait out every ridge of that climb, and one caught cheater forfeits its stake, so mass identities become expensive and slow.
